abstract: Single-cell research is transforming biology and medicine, offering unprecedented insight into health and disease. Yet, the true potential of single-cell data can only be realized when datasets are open, easy to interact with, and accessible to all. We introduce SingloCell (https://singlocell.openscience.mcgill.ca/), an intuitive multimodal single-cell web platform built on three principles: accessibility, interactivity and traceability. SingloCell provides free browser-based access to single-cell datasets and supports user submission of suspension-based transcriptomics, proteomics, chromatin accessibility (ATAC-derived gene activity matrices), immune receptor (BCR, TCR) and multi-omics modalities, as well as spatial datasets. This enables researchers, clinicians, educators, and the broader community to explore high-dimensional datasets without programming expertise. Users can explore and analyse data in real time using tools for differential gene expression, functional enrichment, and pathway visualisation, while also examining pre-computed analyses such as pseudotime trajectories and cell-cell interactions. Datasets can be shared publicly or via unlisted links, and analytical workflows are documented through downloadable receipts.
